title: Vending Machine
context: The canonical state-machine problem. Weak answers model it with booleans scattered across methods; strong answers make the state explicit so impossible transitions are unrepresentable.
statement:
Design the low-level structure of a vending machine controller.

The machine accepts coins and notes, allows the buyer to select a product, dispenses the product, and returns change. It can refuse exact-change-only purchases when it cannot make change. It must track inventory per product slot and report 'sold out'. A restocker can refill slots. An operator can read totals for accounting.

The vending behaviour is a sequence: idle → accepting money → product selected → dispensing → returning change (if any) → idle. Invalid actions (selecting before paying, dispensing twice) must be impossible or handled explicitly.

Your design should make the current machine state explicit and show how a future 'card payment' mode would be added without rewriting the machine.

requirements.text: The machine's operating state must be explicit (idle, has money, product selected, dispensing) rather than implied by scattered booleans.
Money is inserted, tracked, and refundable — including refusing a selection when change cannot be made.
Inventory per product slot: quantity, sold-out detection, and restocking.
Product selection and dispensing are separate steps with invalid-action handling.
Invalid or impossible transitions are rejected explicitly, not silently ignored.
Accounting/totals are visible to an operator without exposing internals of the sales flow.
